yellow_leaves.name: Nitrogen deficiency
yellow_leaves.description: Older leaves turn uniformly pale yellow while new growth stays greener; plants look stunted.
yellow_leaves.treatment: Feed with an organic nitrogen source (compost tea, blood meal, or liquid seaweed) and mulch with compost.
yellow_leaves.prevention: Top-dress beds with compost each season and avoid overwatering, which leaches nitrogen.

yellow_leaves.name: Overwatering / root rot
yellow_leaves.description: Yellow, droopy leaves with persistently soggy soil and a musty smell.
yellow_leaves.treatment: Stop watering, improve drainage, and let the top few centimetres dry before watering again.
yellow_leaves.prevention: Water only when the top 2-3 cm of soil is dry; ensure containers have drainage holes.

yellow_leaves.name: Magnesium deficiency
yellow_leaves.description: Yellowing between the leaf veins (interveinal chlorosis), usually on older leaves first.
yellow_leaves.treatment: Apply an organic Epsom-salts foliar spray or a seaweed feed.
yellow_leaves.prevention: Use a balanced compost and avoid high-potassium feeds that can lock out magnesium.

spots.name: Fungal leaf spot
spots.description: Brown or black spots, often with a yellow halo, spreading in humid conditions.
spots.treatment: Remove affected leaves, improve air flow, and apply an organic copper or bicarbonate spray.
spots.prevention: Water at the base rather than overhead and space plants for airflow.

spots.name: Bacterial spot
spots.description: Water-soaked, angular spots that darken and may ooze.
spots.treatment: Remove infected leaves and apply a copper spray; sterilise tools after use.
spots.prevention: Rotate crops and avoid handling wet plants.

spots.name: Sunscald
spots.description: Dry, pale or brown patches on leaves exposed to intense direct sun.
spots.treatment: Provide shade cloth during the hottest hours.
spots.prevention: Harden off seedlings gradually and site sun-sensitive plants in partial shade.

holes.name: Slugs and snails
holes.description: Large, irregular holes with silvery slime trails, worst after rain or at night.
holes.treatment: Hand-pick at dusk, set beer traps, or apply copper tape around beds.
holes.prevention: Clear debris and water in the morning so surfaces dry by night.

holes.name: Caterpillars
holes.description: Chewed leaves with dark frass (droppings) nearby.
holes.treatment: Hand-pick, or spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis), an organic caterpillar control.
holes.prevention: Use row covers to keep adult moths from laying eggs.

holes.name: Flea beetles
holes.description: Many tiny 'shot-hole' punctures, especially on young seedlings.
holes.treatment: Apply neem oil and protect seedlings with row covers.
holes.prevention: Keep beds weed-free and use a trap crop such as radish.

wilting.name: Underwatering
wilting.description: Dry soil with limp leaves that recover overnight.
wilting.treatment: Give a deep, slow soak at the base and mulch to retain moisture.
wilting.prevention: Water consistently and check soil moisture regularly in warm weather.

wilting.name: Overwatering
wilting.description: Soggy soil with wilting and yellowing leaves that do not recover.
wilting.treatment: Let the soil dry out and improve drainage.
wilting.prevention: Water less often and ensure containers drain freely.

wilting.name: Fusarium / Verticillium wilt
wilting.description: Wilting on one branch or one side of the plant, often despite moist soil.
wilting.treatment: Remove and dispose of the plant (there is no cure); solarise the soil before replanting.
wilting.prevention: Choose resistant varieties and rotate crops.

white_powder.name: Powdery mildew
white_powder.description: White powdery coating on leaf surfaces in warm, humid conditions.
white_powder.treatment: Spray a milk or bicarbonate solution, or neem; prune affected growth.
white_powder.prevention: Improve air flow, space plants, and water at the base.

white_powder.name: Downy mildew
white_powder.description: White or grey fuzz on leaf undersides with yellowing tops.
white_powder.treatment: Remove infected leaves and apply an organic copper spray.
white_powder.prevention: Avoid overhead watering and improve air circulation.

white_powder.name: Mealybugs
white_powder.description: White, cottony clusters on stems and leaf joints (an insect, not a fungus).
white_powder.treatment: Dab with rubbing alcohol and apply neem oil.
white_powder.prevention: Inspect new plants before introducing them.
